title: High‐Performance Bioreceptive Concrete for Vertical Greening: Concept and Design
content: Specially engineered bioreceptive concrete may support the growth of living organisms—such as bryophytes, algae, bacteria, lichens, and fungi—on its surface without degrading its structural integrity. Bioreceptive concrete features a uniquely tailored combination of mechanical, physical, and biological properties (such as improved water retention capacity, optimized pH levels, and a tailored mineral composition) that encourage natural biological colonization, transforming inert surfaces into living, self-sustaining ecosystems. The present study investigates the applicability of high-performance bioreceptive concrete (HPBC) as an external cladding material in building envelopes, specifically for ventilated facades. The prototype ribbed panels were designed and produced from the modified high-performance concrete mix. To enhance the bioreceptivity properties of concrete, a highly water-absorbent mineral, zeolite, was used at different dosage ratios. Several manufacturing techniques and surface treatment methods were investigated for production efficiency, aesthetics, and water retention properties. The results have shown that partial replacement of sand with zeolite may considerably increase short-term water absorption (up to 320%) and reduce bulk weight (up to 13%), without significantly compromising flexural strength. Based on the results of physical and mechanical tests, a perspective HPBC mix was selected for the production of demonstrative wall panels. It was shown that HPBC panels may be designed and manufactured with ornamental rib patterns that serve as both structural elements and water-retention and distribution channels. Eight pilot HPBC panels were installed in a field stand for natural colonization. The study emphasized further critical research directions: accelerated evaluation of bioreceptivity under ideal laboratory conditions and freeze-thaw testing of zeolite-modified HPBC.
